# zero-json

The buffer-direct JSON writer and the strict JSON parser with depth and size caps for zero-server.

[API reference](https://molexxxx.github.io/zero-server/docs/reference/rust/zero_json/index.html) | [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/zero-json) | [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/zero-json)

## The same capability in every language

| Language | Package | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rust | [`zero-json`](https://crates.io/crates/zero-json) | [reference](https://molexxxx.github.io/zero-server/docs/reference/rust/zero_json/index.html), [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/zero-json), [install](https://molexxxx.github.io/zero-server/docs/reference/rust.html#rust-codecs) |
| Rust | [`zero-base64`](https://crates.io/crates/zero-base64) | [reference](https://molexxxx.github.io/zero-server/docs/reference/rust/zero_base64/index.html), [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/zero-base64), [install](https://molexxxx.github.io/zero-server/docs/reference/rust.html#rust-codecs) |
| Rust | [`zero-mime`](https://crates.io/crates/zero-mime) | [reference](https://molexxxx.github.io/zero-server/docs/reference/rust/zero_mime/index.html), [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/zero-mime), [install](https://molexxxx.github.io/zero-server/docs/reference/rust.html#rust-codecs) |

The TypeScript, Python and C# packages of this capability ship in a later release.

The JSON codec of zero-server (RFC 8259).

`Writer` serializes straight into a byte buffer: objects, keys, strings with
the escapes Section 7 requires, integers, floats, arrays, booleans and null,
with no intermediate tree, which is what the json benchmark route and the
tier 2 serializers need. `parse` is the strict parser: it accepts every text
of the Section 2 grammar and nothing else, into the `Value` model of
`zero-core`, under a size cap and a nesting cap (Section 9), decoding strings as
UTF-8 (Section 8.1) with an unpaired surrogate escape refused.

## const `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`

The largest integer a binary64 holds exactly: `2^53 - 1` (RFC 8259 Section
6). Integers past it or past its negation are lossy in JavaScript, which
`BigIntegers::Strings` is for.

```rust
const MAX_SAFE_INTEGER: i64
```
